FILE ASSEMBLY, VERIFICATION AND VALIDATION A. Trkov, IAEA, Vienna, Austria
The ENDF-formatted data from EMPIRE calculation were merged consistently with the resonance data (see description below).
Average number of delayed neutrons and delayed neutron spectra were taken from JENDL-3.3 and extrapolated flat to 60 MeV.
The assembled file was checked according to the IAEA verification procedure [1]. None of the checking codes reported any significant warnings. Comparison with experimental data from EXFOR confirmed that the data are representative of the database on which the evaluation is based. The ACE file for Monte Carlo transport calculations was produced as a result of the checking process, including standard plots. No specific benchmarks sensitive to Pa-231 data were identified, therefore further validation could not be performed. Plots and other details are available on the above-defined web page of the CRP.
[1] A. Trkov: Guidelines for Nuclear Data Verification and Validation, International Atomic Energy Agency, Vienna, Austria, INDC(SEC)-0107, August 2005.

Authors: Roberto Capote (IAEA/NAPC, Nuclear Data Section) Mihaela Sin (University of Bucharest, Romania) Andrej Trkov (IAEA/NAPC, Nuclear Data Section)
EVALUATION PROCEDURE
Adopted procedure is based on careful theoretical analysis utilizing available experimental data and nuclear reaction model calculations.
Available experimental data were interpreted using nuclear reaction model code EMPIRE-2.19b33 by M. Herman et al [He01, He02]. This code integrates into a single system a number of important modules and features, relevant for this evaluation: - Spherical and deformed Optical Model including coupled-channels (ECIS03 by J. Raynal) - Hauser-Feshbach statistical model including HRTW width fluctuation correction - Exciton model with Iwamoto-Harada cluster emission and Kalbach systematic angular distr. (code PCROSS by R.Capote et al) - Complete gamma-ray cascade after emission of each particle, including realistic treatment of discrete transitions - Access to OM segment of the RIPL-2 library [Ri03] - Built-in input parameter files, such as masses, level density, discrete levels, fission barriers and gamma strength functions based on the RIPL-2 library [Ri03] - Automatic retrieval of experimental data from the EXFOR/CSISRS library - ENDF-6 formatting (code EMPEND by A. Trkov) coupled to graphical presentation capabilities (code ZVView by V. Zerkin) through the chain of PrePro codes by R. Cullen - Checking codes (CHECKR, FIZCON, PSYCHE) - Support for NJOY
PARAMETERIZATIONS
Following models and parameters were used in the current evaluation:
Discrete levels were taken from the RIPL-2 level file, based on the 1998 version of ENSDF. EMPIRE-specific level densities Exclusive spectra available up to emission loop # 3 Coupled Channels (ECIS) used for direct inelastic scattering Width fluctuations calculated within HRTW up to 0.90 MeV Exciton model calculations with code PCROSS Cluster emission in terms of the Iwamoto-Harada model Kalbach systematics angular distributions (see RIPL-1) Mean free path parameter in PCROSS set to 1.7 (Recommended ~ 1.5 Max hole number in PCROSS set to 0.20*sqrt(g*U) being U the CN excitation energy Emission width of ejectile 0 from 232Pa multiplied by 1.300 For all nuclei: advanced treatment of fission Prompt fission neutron spectra and nu-bar calculation include contributions from Pa and Th chains (see description of the method in Maslov V.M. et al, Eur.Phys.J.A18(2003)93). Calculations were carried out with a new EMPIRE PFNS module developed by R. Capote and M. Sin. Nu-bar evaluation at thermal energy is based on calculations carried out by A. Tudora, G. Vladuca and F.-J.Hambsch. Above the first fission chance both post-fission and pre-fission neutrons were considered. Prefission neutrons angular distribution assumed anisotropic following (n,xn) distribution. EMPIRE-specific level densities E1 strength function set to MLO1 GDR parameters from RIPL-2/Exp.data+Plujko systematics

RESOLVED RESONANCE PARAMETER S.F. Mughabghab, L. Leal
The resolved MLBW resonance parameters were evaluated by S.F Mughabghab. A bound level is postulated to fit the thermal constants [1]. In addition, to fit a bound coherent scattering amplitude of 9.3 fm, a potential scattering radiu of 10.4 fm was required, which is larger than the systematics in this mass region. With these parameters the following thermal constants are obtained: capture=200.7 b scattering= 11.2 b fission = 0.020 b capture resonance integral=536b including contribution from the unresolved region.
Fission widths above 60 eV that were zero were assigned a width of 5E-6 eV (recommendation by L. Leal).
Some additional reformulation of the parameters was done by L. Leal. The resonance parameters were converted into Reich-Moore formalism an covariances were generated from the quoted uncertainties of the resonance parameters.
[1] S.F. Mughabghab, Atlas of Neutron Resonances, Elsevier,2006.
